curriculum.lesson_evidence: Hot food is kept steaming hot if it will be served soon, or it is cooled quickly and refrigerated. Large deep pots cool slowly in the centre, so leftovers go into shallow containers, uncovered until the steam drops, then covered in the fridge. This is general kitchen guidance, not a promise that every dish is safe. When in doubt, throw it out.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Leftover pasta fills one deep plastic tub and sits out “so the fridge is not warmed”. What is the better cooling method?

FEEDBACK
Split the pasta into shallow containers so the middle cools faster, then refrigerate once it is no longer steaming. Protecting the fridge does not justify an all-night bench stay.

WATCH FOR
Putting a boiling pot straight into the fridge with the lid on and assuming the centre cools at once. The centre can stay warm for a long time.
